title: Cancel Malaysia Day celebration, focus on flood relief – DAP Sabah | Borneo Post Online
text:
Cancel Malaysia Day celebration, focus on flood relief – DAP Sabah | Borneo Post Online
KOTA KINABALU (Sept 15): DAP Sabah called for the cancellation of Malaysia Day celebrations in view of the severe floods and landslides that have struck the whole Sabah including Kota Kinabalu and Penampang, as well as the widespread breakdown of power and water supply on the east coast of Sabah.
Its chairman, Datuk Phoong Jin Zhe, stressed that these cascading crises demand urgent and undivided attention from all levels of government.
He said the situation had been further aggravated by the landslide that brought down the 275kV transmission tower, cutting off electricity supply and triggering widespread disruptions.
At the same time, flash floods have inundated multiple districts, forcing families to evacuate and leaving many with damaged homes and livelihoods.
With clean water supply also affected in several areas, Sabah is facing a compounded humanitarian emergency, he pointed out in a statement on Monday.
DAP Sabah emphasised that in order to truly honour the spirit of Malaysia Day, these disasters must be recognised as a national-level crisis.
The party stressed that unity and patriotism are not expressed merely through parades or ceremonial events, but through decisive action, compassion, and solidarity with fellow Malaysians in distress.
Phoong said the focus of government machinery should be wholly redirected toward relief and recovery efforts.
“This is not the time for celebration. It is the time for mobilisation. The people of Kota Kinabalu, Penampang, and the east coast are in dire need of shelter, food, clean water, medical assistance and immediate restoration of basic utilities. Malaysia Day must be commemorated through service and solidarity, not festivity,” he said.
The party further noted that precedents exist for such a decision. Kuala Lumpur once cancelled Merdeka celebrations in respect of victims of a tragic sinkhole incident in 2024, while Selangor previously called off Aidilfitri celebrations following the devastating blaze in Putra Heights in 2025.
These actions, DAP Sabah stressed, reflected leadership that placed compassion above ceremony — and the same principle should apply in Sabah today.
The party called on both state and federal agencies, including local councils and welfare departments, to intensify their efforts to assist affected families.
Additional allocation of resources, deployment of personnel, and fast-tracked emergency support are urgently required to minimise further hardship.
DAP Sabah also reiterated its readiness to cooperate with relevant authorities, NGOs, and community leaders to coordinate aid distribution and ensure assistance reaches victims without delay.
By calling off Malaysia Day celebrations, DAP Sabah underscored that the most meaningful way to mark this national occasion is by protecting lives, prioritising the welfare of the people, and restoring essential services.
“At this difficult time, channeling all available resources into relief efforts is the truest demonstration of unity and the best way to honour the spirit of Malaysia Day,” said Phoong.
